skill.name: safe-debug
skill.description: Conservative debugging support for deep learning research failures. It helps diagnose tracebacks, CUDA memory errors, checkpoint mismatches, shape issues, NaN losses, and training failures before any code changes are proposed.
skill.summary: Diagnoses deep learning research failures with explicit approval gates before patching.

content.value_statement: Training failures can lead agents into risky patching before the root cause is clear. This skill guides conservative diagnosis, savepoint planning, and approval-based fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies common deep learning failures such as CUDA OOM, checkpoint mismatch, shape mismatch, device mismatch, NaN loss, and file errors.
Creates conservative diagnosis, patch plan, and status outputs under debug_outputs.
Requires explicit approval before repository code changes are made.
Recommends savepoints before medium-risk or high-risk debug changes.
Accepts either inline error text or a text file containing the failure symptom.
Separates debug fixes from changes that affect research meaning or experiment comparability.
limitations: It focuses on deep learning research failures, not general software debugging.
It does not automatically patch code or validate the final fix.
It depends on the quality and completeness of the provided traceback or symptom.
The current instructions reference shared files outside the skill folder and should be packaged locally.

use_cases.title: Triage a Training Crash
use_cases.description: Analyze a pasted traceback and identify the likely failure category before changing experiment code.

use_cases.title: Plan a Minimal Fix
use_cases.description: Generate a patch plan that separates configuration fixes from model or dataset logic changes.

use_cases.title: Control Agent Patching
use_cases.description: Require diagnosis, evidence, savepoint guidance, and user approval before an AI assistant edits files.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Traceback
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-debug to diagnose this traceback. Identify the likely category, explain the evidence, and do not patch code yet: [paste traceback]

prompt_templates.title: Compare Likely Causes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate diagnosis when symptoms are ambiguous.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-debug to compare the top likely causes for this training failure. Rank them by evidence and list the smallest checks before any code change: [paste symptom]

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Patch Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-debug to create a patch plan for this error. Separate configuration fixes, environment checks, and code changes. State whether a savepoint is needed: [paste error]

prompt_templates.title: Audit Research Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for changes that may affect experiment meaning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-debug to audit whether the proposed debug fix changes research comparability. Identify metrics, checkpoints, or dataset assumptions that need verification: [describe fix]

output_examples.input: A CUDA out-of-memory traceback during model training.
output_examples.output: The skill classifies the issue as CUDA OOM, recommends checking batch size and precision settings, and blocks patching until approval.

output_examples.input: A checkpoint load failure with missing and unexpected keys.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a checkpoint mismatch, asks the user to verify model variant assumptions, and recommends a savepoint before compatibility changes.

output_examples.input: A shape mismatch after changing dataset labels.
output_examples.output: The skill narrows the issue to dataset, head dimension, or configuration mismatch and suggests logging boundary shapes before editing model internals.

best_practices: Provide the full traceback, launch command, and recent configuration changes.
Review the diagnosis and patch plan before authorizing edits.
Create a savepoint before fixes that affect checkpoints, model shapes, distributed training, or loss behavior.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for broad refactors or repository walkthroughs without an active failure.
Asking the agent to patch first and explain the diagnosis later.
Treating a passing debug fix as a validated research contribution without checking experiment comparability.

faq.question: Does this skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to diagnose first and require explicit approval before code changes.

faq.question: What types of failures does it recognize?
faq.answer: It recognizes CUDA memory errors, checkpoint mismatches, distributed issues, device mismatches, shape mismatches, NaN losses, and missing files.

faq.question: Can it work with inline error text?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script accepts inline error text or a text file containing the error.

faq.question: Is this useful outside deep learning projects?
faq.answer: Only in limited cases. The guidance and categories are tailored to deep learning research workflows.

faq.question: Why does it recommend savepoints?
faq.answer: Savepoints protect experiments before changes that may affect checkpoints, shapes, loss behavior, or distributed training.

faq.question: What should authors fix before marketplace publication?
faq.answer: They should replace parent-directory references with local bundled files inside the skill package.
